I have combination skin, and acne that affects all regions of my face. Four weeks in, my acne is cleared and I can actually see my freckles instead of acne. Even the little sebaceous glands on my nose are shrinking. LaRoche Posay's Effaclar cleanser appears unassuming, but it's VERY effective!! I've tried dermatologist prescribed treatments, consumer commercial treatments, every brand at "insert other retailer here" that claims to treat acne, whether it's chemical or plant-derived natural treatments, I tried it. If you're looking for perfumey, soft girl vibes, all the fluff, you won't find it here. You'll find a simple but effective acne treatment cleanser. I pair this with LaRoche Posay's daily UV moisturizer and occasionally, the oil based cleanser in the morning if I wake up with dry skin, but otherwise this is it. Simple, effective. You should at least try this, and my biggest tip for anyone looking for an answer to their acne: don't mix a bunch of different products. Some ingredients negate others, some don't react well together. Give a product a trial for about 3-4 weeks, and if it doesn't work, try the next one.

avis.titre: Love this stuff! I even wash my hair with it!
avis.texte: I have super super sensitive, aging skin, and am allergic to "everything." I have fine, curly hair, with some coarse white/greys, that was starting to feel like I could never get it clean. My scalp had all kinds of build up, even though I never apply "products" to my scalp anymore, just shampoo and conditioner. Since silicone seemed to get a bad name in hair care (some silicones are water soluble, and some aren't, and there was no easy way to tell), it seems that instead, everything is formulated with polyquants now. They are similar to silicone, and vary in how easily or how difficult they are to wash off. I have tried everything unscented, clarifying. I went to Aveda and saw all the build up on my scalp. Switching to using this as shampoo has fixed EVERYTHING. It doesn't coat the hair like pretty much everything else does in the name of sealing in something that is supposed to be good for it. (I don't end up with a burned scalp or contact dermatitis on my face or body!) For a while, I used follow-up with the La Roche Posay face wash with nicinamide and glycerin for oily skin as a conditioner. I would comb my hair with it in. But after a while, the glyerin seemed to be a problem. Now, I just wash it with this. My hair does feel a bit squeeky clean when I don't condition it in the shower, but instead, now I use a homemade oil blend of more hemisqualane than squalane, and a few drops of sunflower seed oil when my hair is soaking wet, and as it dries.
